**Finding: deviation (critical) — Section 14.2 (p0054)**

Section 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer in Vendor, giving us only a *revocable, non-transferable* licence lasting only for the Order Form term. That fails the preferred position (we own what we pay for, with Vendor assignment) and also the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense). The perpetual licence in Section 13.2 referenced by Section 14.3 covers only software/Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, so it does not cure either the ownership direction or the revocability.

Sections 14.1 (Customer Data and pre-existing Customer IP), 14.3 (Vendor Technology retention with licence-back) and 14.4 (no joint ownership, feedback rights retained) are acceptable and untouched.

Redline validated (ok:true): 14.2 reversed so Customer owns Deliverables with an irrevocable assignment from Vendor, expressly carving out Vendor Technology, which remains governed by Sections 14.3 and 13.2.
